distinctFrom.because: RET-22 reads a pattern of expected usage not happening across a relationship. This is the non-occurrence of one specific confirmed booking at one specific time, and it is established by exclusion rather than by observing a trend.

title: SCH-180 Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
summary: Recover a commitment we cannot keep, without any of the cost landing on the person who was ready.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-145 handles a generic fulfillment exception. This carries the scheduling-specific recovery: the same time with a different provider, a different time with the same commitment, and the rule that the customer is never recorded as the cause.

title: SUB-161 Continuing relationship created → validate → activate or pending
summary: Keep the existence of a continuing agreement apart from the moment it actually starts running.

distinctFrom.because: REL-91 links two entities: a person to an organisation, a parent account to a child, a representative to the entity they act for. Such a link has no term, nothing to renew and nothing to lapse. What is created here has all three, and it is frequently attached to a link REL-91 created rather than replacing it.

title: SUB-162 Future effective start → wait → revalidate → activate or abort
summary: Activate a future-dated relationship from what is true at the effective time, not from what was true when it was scheduled.

title: SUB-163 Renewal window → eligibility → renew, non-renew or review
summary: Reach a decision about the next term, as a decision - separate from anything that makes the next term real.

distinctFrom.because: This produces a decision. SUB-164 makes the new term exist, which depends on payment, confirmation and eligibility that this journey does not touch. A relationship can be decided-to-renew and still not renew.

title: SUB-164 Renewal execution → financial and dependency check → new term active
summary: Make the new term exist, once the things it depends on have actually happened.

distinctFrom.because: SUB-163 decides. This executes, and it is where renewals actually fail - on payment, on eligibility that moved, on a resource that is no longer available. A decision is not a term.

title: SUB-165 Renewal payment failure → grace or recover → renew or lapse
summary: Decide what the relationship does while a failed renewal payment is being chased, without ending it by reflex.

distinctFrom.because: FIN-134 classifies the payment failure and tries to collect. This decides what the relationship is while that happens - in grace, restricted, pending or lapsing - which is a question about the contract rather than about the money.

title: SUB-166 Plan or terms change request → validate → schedule, apply or reject
summary: Apply an authorized change to a running relationship at the right time, as a delta against whatever is actually there then.

distinctFrom.because: This changes the commercial relationship - the plan, the tier, the scope, the contractual terms. ACC-73 applies whatever entitlement delta results. One is what was agreed; the other is what is switched on.

This changes the authorized terms a continuing relationship runs under. REL-92 changes what the structural relationship between the entities means. A tier change leaves the person exactly as related to the organisation as they were, and a membership type changing leaves the plan exactly as it was priced.

title: SUB-167 Cancellation request → determine effective end → schedule or cancel now
summary: Establish whether and when a relationship will end, while the current term keeps running until it does.

distinctFrom.because: This decides that the relationship will end and when. SUB-168 checks, at that date, whether the decision still applies to the relationship as it then is - which is a different question with a different failure mode.

title: SUB-168 Scheduled cancellation → revalidate at effective time → end or preserve
summary: Stop a scheduled end from executing against a relationship the counterparty has since chosen to keep.

distinctFrom.because: SUB-167 decides the end. This is the guard between that decision and its execution, months later, against a relationship that may have been renewed, upgraded or resubscribed in between.

title: SUB-169 Suspension or hold → restrict relationship → restore or end
summary: Hold a relationship in a state where it cannot operate normally and has not ended.

distinctFrom.because: This is the commercial relationship's suspension state. ACC-78 is what happens to capability and access as a result. A relationship can be suspended for reasons that restrict nothing, and access can be suspended without the contract changing at all.

title: SUB-170 Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
summary: Stop what the relationship was granting, while everything it created keeps its own lifecycle.

distinctFrom.because: A subscription, contract or membership ends here. TRM-106 closes the account relationship entirely. Most people who leave a plan keep their account, and chaining the two treats cancelling a subscription as asking to be removed.

REL-93 ends a structural link between two entities, and what stops is what depended on the link existing. This ends a term, and what stops is what the term was granting. Someone can leave an organisation while the subscription they paid for personally keeps running, and a policy can expire while the person stays exactly as related to the organisation as before.

title: TIM-61 Deadline created → track → complete, escalate or expire
summary: Let a deadline govern the state of one obligation, rather than schedule messages around a date.

distinctFrom.because: A deadline is a moment by which something must be done. An expiry is a moment at which something stops being valid. The first can pass with the obligation intact; the second cannot.

title: TIM-62 Due-state change → recalculate priority → resolve or escalate
summary: Change what an unresolved obligation costs operationally when it becomes due or overdue, rather than only announcing that it has.

title: TIM-63 Expiry approaching → eligibility check → renew, complete or let expire
summary: Use the window before an expiry only where acting inside it could actually change what happens.

distinctFrom.because: This runs while the outcome can still change. TIM-64 runs at the moment it stops being able to. Keeping them apart is what makes expiring and expired different states rather than the same one announced twice.

title: TIM-64 Expiry reached → validate current state → expire, extend or replace
summary: Check what the entity actually is at the moment the expiry fires, before applying anything the timer was written to apply.

title: TIM-65 Grace period entry → temporary continuity → recover or terminate
summary: Keep limited continuity while something recoverable is unresolved, without pretending the normal active state still exists.

distinctFrom.because: Grace is a specific degraded continuity after validity ends, with a recovery condition. TIM-67 is the generic mechanism for any temporary state, most of which are not degradations of anything.

title: TIM-66 Temporary exception → validity window → revert or formalise
summary: Stop an exception granted for a reason from becoming a permanent state nobody remembers deciding on.

distinctFrom.because: An exception departs from a standing policy and carries an authority who granted it. A temporary state is a lifecycle position; it does not necessarily contradict anything.

title: TIM-67 Temporary state → explicit expiry → restore or transition
summary: Give any time-bound state a defined ending, and revalidate before returning anything to what it was.

title: TIM-68 Reversible state → reversal window → confirm or restore
summary: Undo a transition within its window while restoring only what is independently still valid.

title: TIM-69 Expired state → re-entry eligibility → renew, requalify or remain expired
summary: Decide how something expired can become valid again, through the mechanism that actually restores validity rather than by editing the expiry away.

title: TIM-70 Scheduled future transition → validate at execution → apply, cancel or recalculate
summary: Treat a scheduled transition as an intention recorded in the past, and check it against the present before applying it.

distinctFrom.because: An expiry is one specific scheduled transition with entity-specific consequences. This is the general mechanism, and every other scheduled change - a plan change at period end, a future cancellation, a scheduled restriction - runs through it.

title: TRM-101 Identity or entity merge → reconcile → consolidate → verify
summary: Consolidate records that represent one entity, after every dependent state has been reconciled under its own authority rule.

distinctFrom.because: Account consolidation unifies business structure and leaves the people distinct. This consolidates the representations of one entity, which is a decision about identity and carries a far higher evidence bar.

title: TRM-102 Merge conflict → safe state → resolve → continue or abort
summary: Fail safe wherever consolidating would require inventing an authority the system does not have.

title: TRM-103 Account consolidation → dependency reconciliation → unified relationship
summary: Unify business structure across accounts while every person involved stays a separate person.

title: TRM-104 Primary relationship transfer → validate new primary → transfer dependencies
summary: Move a dependent entity to a new primary, carrying only what the primary relationship actually governs.

distinctFrom.because: Changing which primary a dependent hangs from moves a relationship. It consolidates nothing and neither party's identity changes.

title: TRM-105 Role or responsibility handover → effective-time transfer → continue
summary: Move a role between two people at a defined moment, without changing anything before it or rewriting anything behind it.

distinctFrom.because: OWN-54 moves ownership of one work item now. This moves a role and everything it carries at a future effective point, which is why both actors are revalidated when that point arrives rather than when it was scheduled.
REL-94 changes one person's role. This moves a role from one person to another, which means two actors to validate and a set of open work that has to travel intact.

title: TRM-106 Account closure request → validate → resolve blockers → close
summary: End an account relationship once the obligations that legitimately block it are resolved, and end nothing else.

distinctFrom.because: RET-29 completes a subscription cancellation - a commercial relationship ending. An account can be closed with subscriptions running, and a subscription can be cancelled with the account intact.

title: TRM-107 Account closure → reconcile external and commercial dependencies → finalize
summary: Make sure nothing that lives outside the account is assumed to have ended because the account did.

title: TRM-108 Closure completed → wind-down → former or terminal account state
summary: Stop normal account activity while letting the obligations that outlive closure actually finish.

title: TRM-109 Data deletion request → validate scope → hold, delete or retain required data
summary: Decide what a deletion request actually covers, and keep only what an authoritative retention obligation genuinely requires.

distinctFrom.because: Closing an account ends a relationship and requests nothing about data. A deletion request concerns data and says nothing about whether the relationship continues. Either can happen without the other.

title: TRM-110 Data deletion execution → propagate → verify or reconcile failure
summary: Carry a deletion through every system it has to reach, and keep any part that did not arrive visible.
